newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-MARIO LEMIEUX COMPLETES REGULAR-SEASON CAREER.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-MARIO LEMIEUX COMPLETES REGULAR-SEASON CAREER.

text.p: Mario Lemieux completed his regular-season career with two assists as Pittsburgh lost to the Boston Bruins 7-3 Sunday, dropping the Penguins into a sixth-place finish in the Eastern Conference on the final day of the NHL regular season.

Jozef Stumpel had a career-high five points as the Bruins assured Pittsburgh of meeting third-seeded Philadelphia in the first round of the playoffs. A win would have put the Penguins into fifth place and a first-round meeting with Florida.

Lemieux, who had announced he will retire following the playoffs, captured his sixth scoring title in his 13th NHL season with 50 goals and 72 assists for 122 points in 76 games. His two assists tied him with the Rangers' Wayne Gretzky for the league lead.
In 745 regular-season games, Lemieux tallied 613 goals and 881 assists for 1,494 points, good for sixth on the all-time list.
Following the game, the Bruins players congratulated Lemieux at centre ice as he received a standing ovation from the fans at the FleetCenter.

"I knew that it was coming to an end," Lemieux said. "I've been looking forward to the playoffs for a long time now. In the last few games of the season, it has been a lot of fun. Many of the opponents have given me gifts and I've received some outstanding ovations."
Stumpel had two goals and three assists, Landon Wilson added two goals and an assist and Ted Donato set up four scores for Boston, which failed to make the playoffs for the first time in 30 seasons.
The Bruins, who lost 10 of their final 12 games, finished with the league's worst record (26-47-9).

In Philadelphia, John LeClair tied it with his 50th goal and Trent Klatt scored the game-winner on the power play with 1:34 remaining as the Flyers rallied for four third-period goals and a 5-4 victory over the New Jersey Devils.
The final regular-season game for both teams lost most of its meaning when Philadelphia tied Montreal on Saturday, giving New Jersey the top seed in the Eastern Conference.

"We cared tonight, but we just didn't show it and that's our fault," Devils winger Bill Guerin said. "The way we played speaks for itself and it's not good. We're going to have to pick up against Montreal."
The Devils, who will play Montreal in the Eastern Conference quarterfinals, stormed to a 4-1 lead after two periods.

But the Devils lost the momentum late in the second period when left wing Dave Andreychuk suffered non-displaced fracture of his left ankle. He was hooked to the ice by rookie defenceman Janne Niinimaa and is expected to miss two to four weeks.
In Colorado, Rob Blake's goal with 9:23 remaining broke a third-period tie and Glen Murray scored twice as the Los Angeles Kings defeated the Avalanche 4-2.
Ray Ferraro had the other goal for the Kings, who finished 28-43-11 and missed the playoffs for the fourth straight year since advancing to the Stanley Cup Finals in 1993.

Keith Jones and Jon Klemm tallied for Colorado, which won the President's Trophy as the NHL's top team in the regular season and will begin defence of its Stanley Cup championship against Chicago in the Western Conference quarterfinals.

In Dallas, Eric Daze recorded his first career hat trick and had an assist as the Chicago Blackhawks topped the Stars 5-2. Jeff Shantz added a goal and an assist and James Black also scored for Chicago.

Pat Verbeek and Todd Harvey tallied for Dallas, which finished second in the Western Conference and plays seventh-seeded Edmonton in the first round.The Stars went 1-3-2 in their final six games of the season following an 11-game unbeaten streak.
In Detroit, the St. Louis Blues clinched sixth place in the Western Conference and a playoff rematch with the Red Wings with a 3-1 victory.
Stephane Matteau had a shorthanded goal and an assist for the Blues, who extended Detroit to double-overtime in the seventh game before losing in last year's Western Conference semifinals.
St. Louis, which got 23 saves from Grant Fuhr, would have drawn Dallas as its first-round opponent with a loss.
In Buffalo, rookie Jaroslav Svejkovsky recorded his first career four-goal game, leading the Washington Capitals to an 8-3 victory over the playoff-bound Sabres.

Svejkovsky, a 20-year-old left wing who was the second of Washington's first-round picks in the 1996 draft, tallied twice in the first period and added two more in the third to complete the Capitals' second four-goal game of the season.
Peter Bondra, who got his 46th of the season in the first period, scored four times against Colorado on March 6.
The Sabres face Ottawa in the playoffs.
Washington, eliminated from playoff contention on Saturday, closed the season with a three-game winning streak.
In Hartford, the Whalers closed out their history in Connecticut as Sean Burke made 38 saves in a 2-1 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning.
The Whalers and the Lightning were eliminated from playoff contention on Saturday night.
The Whalers will move to an as yet undetermined location after playing in the NHL since 1979-80 as one of four former World Hockey Association franchises accepted into the league.
